parties.petitioner: In Re Recruitment Of Visually Impaired In Judicial Services
parties.respondent: The Registrar General, The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh & Ors.

summary: The case addresses systemic exclusion of visually impaired and PWD candidates from judicial services in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. Issues include constitutional validity of rules barring PWD candidates, discrimination under Articles 14, 15, and 16, alignment with RPwD Act, 2016, and permissibility of relaxed selection criteria. The Court adopted a rights-based approach, emphasized duty to provide reasonable accommodation, rejected notions of incapacity based on disability, and held that indirect discrimination violates fundamental rights. Reference made to international conventions and best practices to support inclusion.
legal_provisions_cited: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
final_judgment: The Court held that exclusion of visually impaired and PWD candidates from judicial service recruitment is unconstitutional, discriminatory, and violative of the RPwD Act, 2016. It directed state authorities and high courts to ensure reasonable accommodations, permit relaxation in qualifying criteria, and adopt inclusive policies for PWD candidates in judicial appointments.
